page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel processor cores running two threads per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a substantial shared L3 cache of 260 MB. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8). The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. While single-threaded metrics such as stress-ng single-core (1652.79) and Geekbench single-core (1865.0) fall within the middle tier, the instance achieves top-quartile performance in multi-threaded metrics, scoring 16013.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block memory transfers are notably efficient, delivering 211.52 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 99.63 GB/sec in write bandwidth. Static web serving throughput also registers in the upper 25% at 44.06 GB/sec. For AI inference tasks leveraging AMX and AVX-512 vector units, generation on small models (135M) reaches a strong 296.22 tokens/sec, though performance scales down significantly on larger architectures, dropping to 2.31 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models.

Without bundled local disk storage or GPU acceleration, storage relies on external network volumes, making network I/O considerations critical for data-intensive setups. The instance provides balanced cost efficiency for enterprise compute scenarios by pairing solid multi-core density with high uncached memory bandwidth. It is suited for multi-threaded compilation, web traffic serving, containerized enterprise workloads, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and lightweight edge CPU inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 Intel physical cores on x86_64 architecture, coupled with 128.0 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. It contains no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reflect strong multi-core scalability and high uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 211.52 GB/sec read and 99.63 GB/sec write throughput, alongside upper-quartile static web serving performance at 44.06 GB/sec. Single-core execution and database operations remain within middle-tier ranges, while CPU-based inference performs well on small models but drops on larger parameter networks. This configuration is aligned with enterprise application hosting, high-throughput web serving, CI/CD compilation, and in-memory caching.
